lines.trans: We have exactly ten minutes before the cake cools down and rejects any warm glaze!
Grab your purse, Nour! The corner shop next to the clock tower sells local honey!

words.gram: definite feminine singular noun, with عال- (on/at the)

lines.trans: I am running! Keep the cake warm, Salma, and tell Mazen to wait patiently!
Run like the wind, Nour! A perfect historic recipe depends entirely on your speedy feet!
Good afternoon, Rami! I need a jar of your best golden honey, faster than lightning!
Whoa, Nour! Are you chasing a thief, or did someone accidentally eat a raw hot pepper?

words.gram: definite masculine singular noun, with بال- (in/with the)

lines.trans: Neither! We are baking the thirty-year-old mystery cake and the honey jar is empty!

words.gram: m sg construct noun with w- (and)

lines.trans: Oh, a culinary emergency! Here is a fresh jar of spring blossom honey, on the house.

words.gloss: please go ahead / here you are!

lines.trans: You are a lifesaver, Rami! We will save you a slice if Mazen does not eat it all!
Wait—do not just brush it on plain! Read the botanical book first!

Trust me! Tell Suad to smell the paper where the recipe card rested!

lines.trans: What book? Salma is melting it in a pot the second I sprint through the courtyard gate!
Trust me! Tell Suad to smell the paper where the recipe card rested!
Goodbye!

meanings.note: Elative form of حسن (hasan), used for comparison.

examples.trans: This is better than that.

examples.text: صحتي صارت أحسن بكتير بعد ما ارتحت يومين.
examples.trans: My health got much better after I rested for two days.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باكل, بياكل).

examples.trans: The brothers are eating lemon cake in the courtyard.
We ate a hot breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: أنا وإياك رح نخلص المشروع قبل يوم الخميس.
examples.trans: You and I will finish the project before Thursday.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Used as a question word or indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Which car do you prefer?

examples.text: بأي ساعة رح يبلش الاجتماع اليوم؟
examples.trans: At what hour is the meeting going to start today?

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Second person masculine singular pronoun.

examples.trans: Where do you live?

examples.text: إنت اللي رسمت الخريطة هاي بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Are you the one who drew this map by hand?

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعتمد, بيعتمد).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We rely on Nour at reception.

meanings.note: Command to a female to read.

examples.trans: Read the lesson out loud.

examples.text: اقرأي البطاقة بصوت عالي عشان كلنا نسمع.
examples.trans: Read the card out loud so all of us can hear.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: Recipe or medical prescription.

examples.trans: This recipe for making knafeh is wonderful.

examples.text: أعطاني الصيدلاني الدوا حسب الوصفة اللي كتبها الدكتور.
examples.trans: The pharmacist gave me the medicine according to the prescription the doctor wrote.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببيع, بيبيع).

examples.trans: The hardware shop sells this size.
I thought it was lost when we sold the house!

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical tower, a skyscraper, or an astrological sign.

examples.trans: This is the highest tower in the city.

examples.text: برج الساعة القديم مبين من فوق السطوح.
examples.trans: The old clock tower is visible from the rooftop.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببرد, بيبرد).

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the rack right now.
The radiator is starting to get cold at the bottom.

meanings.note: Flash of lightning in a storm, often paired with رعد ('thunder').

examples.text: شفنا برق قوي ورا قزاز الباب.
examples.trans: We saw bright lightning behind the door glass.

examples.text: بعد البرق بثواني، سمعنا صوت الرعد.
examples.trans: Seconds after the lightning, we heard the roll of thunder.

meanings.note: From بلد ('country, town'); prized on Jordanian market stalls for local olive oil, honey, lemons, and thyme.

examples.text: عسل بلدي من جبال عجلون ريحته بتشهي.
examples.trans: Local honey from the Ajloun hills smells delicious.
We bought yellow local lemons for tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from تاريخ (history), agreeing with الساحة.

examples.text: وسط البلد فيه مباني تاريخية عمرها أكتر من مية سنة.
examples.trans: Downtown has historic buildings that are over a hundred years old.

examples.text: المدرج الروماني معلم تاريخي مهم بعمان.
examples.trans: The Roman Theater is an important historic landmark in Amman.

meanings.note: The feminine form of the Levantine possessive marker.

examples.trans: Reem's bag is lost.

examples.text: العلبة تبعت الشاي الأخضر عالرف التاني.
examples.trans: The green tea tin is on the second shelf.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: His age is now thirty years.

examples.text: ضلينا تلاتين دقيقة بنستنى الكيكة تبرد.
examples.trans: We spent thirty minutes waiting for the cake to cool.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a wallet or handbag/purse.

examples.text: خدي جزدانك يا نور وانزلي عالدكانة.
examples.trans: Grab your purse, Nour, and run down to the shop.
I left my wallet on the table by the door.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Sit next to your brother.
We set the trays next to the fountain in the shade.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: With possessive endings, حال acts as 'myself/yourself/itself' (لحاله by itself, لا تغلبي حالك don't tire yourself).

examples.trans: The door opened by itself from the wind.
How are you doing today?

meanings.note: Commonly used in expressions like حالة طوارئ (emergency).

examples.text: عسل المونة خلص، وهاي حالة طوارئ بالمطبخ!
examples.trans: The pantry honey ran out, and this is a kitchen emergency!

examples.text: حالة الطقس بكرة رح تكون دافية وصافية.
examples.trans: Tomorrow's weather condition will be warm and clear.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Is anyone here?

examples.text: في حدا بعرف وين نحفظت الخريطة؟
examples.trans: Does anyone know where the map was stored?

meanings.note: Colloquial noun widely used across Jordanian and Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ليش بتركضي هيك، عم تلحقي حرامي؟
examples.trans: Why are you running like that, are you chasing a thief?

examples.text: الحرامي هرب قبل ما يجي الحارس.
examples.trans: The thief fled before the guard arrived.

meanings.note: Also used in the warm hospitality phrase على حسابنا ('on our tab / on the house').

examples.trans: The bill is thirty-eight dinars.
The first coffee today is on the house!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The weather today is very warm.

examples.text: الحليب الدافي بسكر الخميرة وبخليها تتفاعل.
examples.trans: Warm milk activates the yeast and helps it rise.

meanings.note: Form II transitive verb (contrast دفي 'to become warm').

examples.text: دفي الكيكة عالفرن لبين ما أرجع بالعسل.
examples.trans: Keep the cake warm on the stove until I get back with the honey.

examples.text: دفينا الشاي عالنار عشان الجو بارد.
examples.trans: We warmed the tea on the fire because the weather is cold.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دكاكين.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I bought milk and bread from the shop.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ذهب (gold); also pronounced دهبي in everyday Jordanian.

examples.text: اخبزي الكيكة ليصير لونها ذهبي حلو.
examples.trans: Bake the cake until its colour turns a lovely golden.
She won a gold medal in the cooking competition.

meanings.note: Form II transitive verb; also pronounced دوّب in casual speech.

examples.text: سلمى رح تذوب العسل والزبدة بطنجرة صغيرة.
examples.trans: Salma is going to melt the honey and butter in a small pot.

examples.text: ذوبنا السكر بالمي الدافية قبل ما نخلطه.
examples.trans: We dissolved the sugar in warm water before mixing it.

meanings.note: Active participle of ركض; commonly used in Levantine for progressive action ('I am running').

examples.text: أنا راكضة عالدكانة أشتري عسل وراجعة فورا!
examples.trans: I am running to the shop to buy honey and coming right back!

examples.text: شفته راكض بالشارع عشان يلحق الباص.
examples.trans: I saw him running down the street to catch the bus.

meanings.note: One of the four seasons: صيف summer, خريف autumn, شتا winter, ربيع spring.

examples.trans: Spring in Amman is short and lovely.
In spring we go out to the hills.

meanings.note: Feminine body-part noun in Levantine Arabic (رجلك اليمين 'your right foot').

examples.text: ارفعي رجلك عالمخدة وارتاحي نص ساعة.
examples.trans: Prop your foot up on the pillow and rest for half an hour.

examples.text: حطيت كيس تلج ملفوف بمنشفة على رجلي.
examples.trans: I placed an ice pack wrapped in a towel on my foot.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: Standard Form I verb.

examples.text: إذا بردت الكيكة رح ترفض طبقة العسل.
examples.trans: If the cake cools down it will reject the honey glaze.

examples.text: رفض ياخد المصاري وقال إنها على حساب المحل.
examples.trans: He refused to take the money and said it was on the house.

meanings.note: Grammatically feminine noun in Arabic (often with plural رياح).

examples.text: اركضي متل الريح يا نور عشان نلحق الكيكة!
examples.trans: Run like the wind, Nour, so we catch the cake in time!
The strong wind moved the courtyard lanterns.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركض, بيركض).

examples.text: اركضي بسرعة قبل ما يصحوا الضيوف!
examples.trans: Run fast before the guests wake up!
You ran across half the town this morning.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: Put the chair in the corner.
The chest is placed in the northern corner of the room.

meanings.note: Singular noun of unity with ta marbuta; collective noun is زهر (flowers). Also used for cauliflower in Levantine food contexts.

examples.text: في زهرة بيضا مرسومة على غلاف الكتاب.
examples.trans: There is a white flower drawn on the cover of the book.
The garden is full of colourful blossoms in spring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: I've been waiting for you for an hour.

examples.text: المكتبة بتفتح كمان ساعة، خلينا نستنى بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The library opens in another hour; let us wait in the garden.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: This car is this year's model.

examples.text: مرّت سنة كاملة على آخر زيارة للمزرعة.
examples.trans: A whole year has passed since the last visit to the farm.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for 'gentleman' or formal 'Mr.' (plural: سادة).

examples.text: هادا السيد الوقور جنب البوابة وسيم كتير!
examples.trans: That distinguished gentleman by the gate is very handsome!
Mr. Mazen welcomes guests with a smile.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial Jordanian noun for a broken piece, slice, or scrap of paper, bread, or stone.

examples.text: لقينا شقفة ورق صغيرة تحت الباب.
examples.trans: We found a small scrap of paper under the door.

examples.text: اقسم الكيكة وعطي كل واحد شقفة متساوية.
examples.trans: Cut the cake and give everyone an equal piece.

meanings.note: Feminine imperative of شمّ (to smell), addressing Salma.

examples.text: شمّي ريحة القرفة والهيل طالعة من الفرن!
examples.trans: Smell the scent of cinnamon and cardamom coming out of the oven!

examples.text: بحب أشمّ هوا نضيف بالحديقة الصبح.
examples.trans: I love breathing in fresh air in the garden in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your patience with us.
Patience is the key to relief.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طازجة, plural: طازجين).

examples.trans: Morning bread is fresh and hot!
Fresh orange juice and fresh cake.

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine kitchen noun for a cooking pot or saucepan.

examples.text: حطي الطنجرة الكبيرة عالنار عشان نطبخ المقلوبة.
examples.trans: Put the big pot on the stove so we can cook maqluba.

examples.text: غطّي الطنجرة وخلي المي تغلي شوي.
examples.trans: Cover the pot and let the water boil for a bit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طوارئ.

examples.trans: We have a small emergency in the kitchen!
The emergency key hangs beside the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: The time is ten o'clock right now.
The shop closes at ten o'clock at night.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: The car is at the door.

examples.text: التقينا عند برج الساعة الساعة عشرة.
examples.trans: We met by the clock tower at ten o'clock.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غامضة, plural: غامضين).

examples.trans: Why did you leave a mysterious note on the door?
We finally found out who the mysterious guest is.

meanings.note: Used as noun in بالغلط ('by mistake') and عالغلط ('for the mistake'), and invariable predicate 'wrong' (في شي غلط something is wrong).

examples.trans: He took the other suitcase by mistake.
Sorry for the mistake, my apologies.

meanings.note: Used to describe an empty container or a person who has free time.

examples.trans: I am free today in the afternoon.

examples.text: الرف الفوقاني فاضي، بنقدر نحط العلبة عليه.
examples.trans: The top shelf is empty; we can put the tin on it.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine noun for bell peppers and mild peppers, contrasted with فلفل (black or hot pepper).

examples.trans: We chopped green and red bell peppers for the salad.

examples.text: سلة الخضار فيها فليفلة طازجة من المزرعة.
examples.trans: The vegetable basket has fresh bell peppers from the farm.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.trans: I have to arrive before five o'clock.

examples.text: غسلنا الفواكه منيح قبل ما نقطعها للتذوق.
examples.trans: We washed the fruit thoroughly before slicing it for the tasting.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: The weather was cold yesterday.

examples.text: الطعم كان متوازن كتير بين العسل والليمون.
examples.trans: The flavour was very well balanced between the honey and lemon.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: All people love summer.

examples.text: كل بطاقة بالعلبة بتحكي عن نبتة عطرية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every card in the tin talks about a different aromatic plant.

meanings.note: Adverbial accusative of كلي (total); frequently paired with negations like مش كليا (not completely).

examples.text: طعم القرفة مختلف كليا عن طعم الزيزفون.
examples.trans: The taste of cinnamon is completely different from linden.

examples.text: نسيت الموضوع كليا مع عجقة التحضير.
examples.trans: I completely forgot about the matter in the rush of preparation.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.trans: I made a delicious chocolate cake.

examples.text: كيكة التوت اللي عملتها سلمى طلعت خفيفة وهشة.
examples.trans: The berry cake that Salma made turned out light and fluffy.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, I don't want to go today.

examples.text: لا تنسوا تطفيوا الفرن بعد ما تخلصوا الخبيز.
examples.trans: Do not forget to turn off the oven after you finish baking.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلحق, بيلحق).

examples.trans: Follow me quickly to the third floor!

examples.text: لحقنا دكان الخردوات أول ما فتح.
examples.trans: We caught the hardware shop right as it opened.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from مثال (example, model); describes ideal timing, conditions, or results.

examples.text: حرارة الجو اليوم مثالية للجلسة بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The weather today is ideal for sitting in the garden.

examples.text: هادا المكان مثالي لتخبية صندوق الكنز.
examples.trans: This spot is ideal for hiding the treasure box.

meanings.note: Passive participle indicating that an object has been set down or positioned somewhere.

examples.trans: The key is placed on the table.

examples.text: المرطبان الدهبي محطوط على أعلى رف بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: The golden jar is placed on the highest shelf in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for any retail shop or spot (pl. محلات).

examples.trans: Below is the signature of the antique shop.
There's a pastry shop next to the house.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a glass jam, honey, or olive jar (dual مرطبانين, plural مرطبانات).

examples.trans: We lined the jars of jam and honey up on the shelf.
Open the new jar of honey for breakfast.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Form IV active participle of أنقذ (to rescue); plural منقذين.

examples.text: إجا رامي بالمفتاح الاحتياطي وكان المنقذ بالوقت الصح.
examples.trans: Rami arrived with the spare key and was the rescuer just in time.

examples.text: الكل شكر المنقذ اللي لاقى الخريطة الضائعة.
examples.trans: Everyone thanked the rescuer who found the lost map.

meanings.note: Generic noun for plants and flora; plural نباتات.

examples.text: الدفتر فيها رسومات عن كل نبات بالحديقة.
examples.trans: The notebook has drawings of every plant in the garden.
We watered the aromatic plants before sunset.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of نيء (dropping final hamza); describes unbaked batter or undercooked food.

examples.text: العجين لسا ني بنص الصينية، بده كمان عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: The batter is still raw in the middle of the tin; it needs ten more minutes.
Do not eat potatoes while they are raw.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: This boy is very smart.

examples.text: هاد المحل ببيع أطيب كنافة نابلسية بعمان.
examples.trans: This shop sells the best Nabulsi kunafa in Amman.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: اشتريت كتاب واحد بس من المعرض لأنه كان غالي.
examples.trans: I bought just one book from the fair because it was expensive.

وثق.gloss: to trust; to have confidence in

meanings.en: to trust; to have confidence in
meanings.note: Form I assimilated verb (root و-ث-ق, losing initial w- in the imperfect: يثق / بثق); takes بـ or في.

examples.text: أنا بثق بذوق سلمى واختيارها للمكونات.
examples.trans: I trust Salma's palate and her choice of ingredients.

examples.text: الكل وثق بالخريطة القديمة وتبع الخطوات.
examples.trans: Everyone trusted the old map and followed the steps.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: Quintessential Jordanian exclamation of astonishment, disbelief, or sudden surprise (pronounced wal).

examples.text: ول! كل هادا الحبر انكب عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Whoa! All this ink spilled onto the table?
No way, could you really have finished the tasting that fast?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.
